name: Canvas Scraps
summary: At Razor Hill, Furl Scornbrow gathers Canvas Scraps to make travel sacks for new Horde recruits. The cloth comes from human invaders and centaur tribes in Durotar.

sections.title: Trophies of Durotar's Enemies
sections.body: Kul Tiras marines and sailors carry canvas along Durotar’s eastern shore. Their gear and sails leave scraps behind. Inland, Kolkar centaur reuse coarse cloth taken from supply caravans and past conflicts. Their camps and gear hold scraps that can be salvaged.

sections.title: A Veteran's Craft
sections.body: Furl Scornbrow watches for invaders from the Razor Hill watchtower. The aging veteran has left his fighting days behind, but puts salvaged enemy cloth to use. He stitches it into sturdy carrying bags for younger soldiers, helping the new generation defend the Horde’s borders.

faq.q: Where do Canvas Scraps come from?
faq.answer: Canvas Scraps come from human and centaur foes across Durotar. Kul Tiras forces at Tiragarde Keep and along the eastern shore carry them, as do Kolkar centaur drudges and outrunners near their inland camps.

faq.q: Why does Furl Scornbrow want these scraps?
aliases: what are canvas scraps used for
faq.answer: Furl Scornbrow is an aging Orc veteran in the Razor Hill watchtower who can no longer fight on the front lines. He sews the salvaged cloth into traveling sacks for young adventurers.

faq.q: Why do the Kul Tiras troops and centaur carry canvas?
faq.answer: Kul Tiras troops came to Durotar aboard warships and keep seaside camps, where sailcloth and woven canvas are everyday essentials. Kolkar centaur get coarse fabrics by raiding caravans, scavenging coastlines, and plundering travelers across the arid plains.

angles.text: Each scrap taken from Kul Tiras invaders or Kolkar raiders helps supply new defenders answering Thrall’s call across Durotar.
Warriors gather woven canvas as raw salvage, and the rugged cloth can be made into practical bags for the harsh desert.
